summary: Discovery focused on security posture for evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Primary concerns: SOC 2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML and RBAC integration, audit log retention and export, encryption/KMS controls, data residency and retention policy, and VPC/on-prem network details. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share compliance artifacts and architecture diagram; schedule deeper security review.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-02-12 15:00 PST
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Mark Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Acme SecOps), Carlos Mendes (CTO), Ethan Liu (Procurement)

[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro from our side, I'm Lena, AE at Redwood, with Mark Chen who is our Solutions Engineer.
[00:12] Mark Chen: Hey team. we'll dive into the security posture questions you sent over, and try to map them to hosted, dedicated and private options.
[00:20] Priya Nair: Hi, thanks. I, uh, I'm Priya, security lead. we've got a checklist — SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, SSO via SAML, RBAC, audit logs retention, KMS integration and data retention policies. also concerned about network controls if we go private or dedicated.
[00:40] Carlos Mendes: And I'm Carlos, CTO. from infra standpoint latency and cost matter but security is a blocker for procurement.
[00:48] Ethan Liu: Ethan from procurement, will be owning contracting.
[00:52] Mark Chen: Great. starting with SOC 2 and ISO — Redwood does maintain SOC 2 Type II, and we have ISO artifacts; we'll share redacted reports. For hosted customers we provide SOC 2 attestations; for Dedicated and Private deployments we provide additional documentation and support for audits.
[01:20] Priya Nair: Can you confirm scope? like is data in customer models or logs included in the SOC scope? we've had vendors where log ingestion was out of scope.
[01:33] Lena Park: Good question — generally our hosting environment and control plane are in scope. customer data handling is described in the AOCs; for Dedicated we can discuss scoping adjustments and contractual commitments. we'll send the AOC and a scoping note.
[01:50] Priya Nair: Ok, and ISO? we need a high-level statement of control mapping.
[01:55] Mark Chen: Yep, we can provide an ISO 27001 statement of applicability and a mapping matrix to common control families; again for Private deployments we can supply more detail.
[02:10] Carlos Mendes: On auth — SSO via SAML is must-have. can you support OIDC, SAML, SCIM provisioning?
[02:18] Mark Chen: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning today; OIDC is supported for some flows. There are enterprise SAML connectors in Console and RBAC roles down to token-level permissions.
[02:33] Priya Nair: How granular is RBAC? can we lock down model access per-team and prevent developers from exporting keys?
[02:40] Mark Chen: RBAC is role-based and can be applied per-route and per-model. We have admin, dev, read-only, and token-scoped permissions. there are some UI caveats — we'll send a role matrix.
[02:55] Priya Nair: Audit logs — we need immutable audit logs for 1 year and ability to export. is that possible?
[03:03] Lena Park: Audit logs are available via our console with export to S3 for hosted and Dedicated. For Private, logs can be forwarded to your SIEM. retention windows are configurable; for hosted there are default retention policies but add-ons allow longer retention.
[03:21] Ethan Liu: Any tamper-evidence? chain or checksum?
[03:25] Mark Chen: We provide append-only event stores and hashed entries; for high-assurance customers we can set up streaming to their secure bucket or SIEM for tamper-evidence.
[03:36] Priya Nair: Encryption — at rest and in transit, and key management. we use a customer-managed KMS and need HSM-backed keys in some cases.
[03:45] Mark Chen: In transit is TLS 1.2+; at rest we encrypt with AES-256. We support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private. For hosted we offer a stricter option where CMKs can be used — HSM-backed where supported by the cloud provider.
[04:04] Carlos Mendes: What about model caching/kv cache — does any customer data persist in caches that could be read by others?
[04:12] Mark Chen: Good callout. we use partitioned caches per-tenant and prefix eviction; KV caches are scoped to tenant and not shared. For sensitive workloads we can disable caching or ensure encryption of cache shards.
[04:28] Priya Nair: Data residency and retention — we have EU customers, need EU residency for data at rest in some cases. can you guarantee region-specific storage?
[04:37] Lena Park: Yes, region pinning is available for Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports region selection for data residency in our EU regions; we can document where logs, models, and backups reside.
[04:50] Priya Nair: Do you retain prompts and model outputs by default? and what's the retention period and deletion process?
[04:57] Mark Chen: By default hosted stores transcripts for X days (we'll confirm exact retention), but customers can opt-out of retention for PII-sensitive workloads. For Dedicated/Private customers data persists per their retention config. Deletion is soft delete plus secure wipe for backups. We'll share the retention policy doc.
[05:18] Priya Nair: Legal will want contractual language about data deletion and breach notification timelines.
[05:24] Ethan Liu: yes, 72-hour notification for incidents is typical requirement.
[05:28] Lena Park: We include standard incident SLA clauses; we can surface the security addendum and incident response playbook.
[05:35] Carlos Mendes: Network controls — if we go Dedicated we'd like VPC peering or private link. what's supported?
[05:42] Mark Chen: We support VPC peering, PrivateLink equivalents, and for Private deployments we can do on-prem installations or customer-managed network connections. we'll share network diagrams and required firewall rules.
[06:00] Priya Nair: For audits we may need direct access to logs and control evidence; can you provide support for that?
[06:07] Mark Chen: Yes, for enterprise customers we provide audit assistance, evidence packages, and runbook walkthroughs; for Private deployments we can provide on-site support as needed.
[06:18] Priya Nair: Are there any known gaps in the controls we should be aware of?
[06:22] Lena Park: There are some hosted feature limits — e.g., most CMK integrations and full log streaming are more mature on Dedicated/Private. we'll call those out in the artifact bundle.
[06:33] Carlos Mendes: Any downstream compliance certifications like FedRAMP or HIPAA?
[06:38] Mark Chen: We are not FedRAMP-authorized yet; we do have HIPAA support via BAA for specific offerings — we'll clarify which tiers are in scope.
[06:49] Priya Nair: Who will be our day-2 contact for security issues?
[06:53] Lena Park: You'll have an assigned CSM and a technical account manager for Dedicated/Private customers; SEs can be on call during onboarding.
[07:02] Ethan Liu: Pricing — security add-ons between hosted and dedicated will affect cost. can you send pricing for retention/add-on?
[07:08] Lena Park: yes we'll include pricing tiers for extended retention, dedicated KMS support, and premium support.
[07:16] Mark Chen: I'll also propose a pilot: short Dedicated trial for benchmarking and a security review with your SecOps.
[07:24] Priya Nair: Sounds good. we'll need the SOC 2 and ISO docs and the network diagram to evaluate.
[07:31] Lena Park: Action recap — we'll send SOC 2 AOC, ISO summary, role matrix, network diagram, retention policy, and pricing addendum.
[07:40] Carlos Mendes: timeline — we are targeting vendor approval by end of March, so two to three weeks for the security review would be ideal.
[07:49] Lena Park: understoood. we'll try to get initial artifacts within 48 hours, schedule the deeper review for week of 2/17.
[07:57] Priya Nair: ok thanks, appreciate it.
[08:00] Ethan Liu: thanks everyone.
[08:05] Mark Chen: thanks all — we'll follow up with the docs and a calendar invite for the security deep dive.

Notes: transcript has occasional mishears and truncated words — this is typical ASR output. References to "AOC" (attestation of compliance), "CMK" (customer-managed keys), "KV cache" and "VPC peering." Some product names may have been transcribed slightly wrong.
